action: opened the order: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.
Delight: proposed Unsent, Second Thoughts, Famous Last Words
person at the terminal: proposed Stakes (stakes-widget), Squiggle (squiggle-widget), Strays (strays-widget)
Untapped capability: proposed Margin, Pointer, Doubt
took the order at ideation
stamped reject on "Pointer": The same idea as Squiggle in this round, minus the paint in the prompt box and the fix on click, so it is the weaker variation of its own sibling.

stamped reject on "Doubt": Deciding which hedges the reply 'addressed' by a phrase list and word overlap will be wrong often enough that the card cannot be trusted, and it has nothing to read when thinking is off or summarised.
stamped reject on "Famous Last Words": A narrow cut of insight-widget (prompting habits against turn outcomes) with a coloured word added; the inventor ranked it last for the same reason.
stamped reject on "Second Thoughts": Not chosen: a charming read of the thinking stream, but it gives the person nothing to act on and is empty whenever thinking is off or summarised.

stamped reject on "Unsent": Not chosen: new and funny once, but it keeps what the person chose to delete, changes no decision, and cannot yet tell a swallowed draft from history recall or a cleared box.

stamped reject on "Strays": Not chosen: useful, but it rests on parsing lsof and netstat per platform every turn and on killing processes by pid, a heavier and riskier build than Stakes for a quieter payoff.

stamped reject on "Squiggle": Not chosen: the strongest runner-up, but picking out which typed words are meant as file or branch names will misfire, and @-completion already covers the path case; worth a later order.

stamped reject on "Margin": Not chosen: a real new interaction, but it works only in fullscreen, needs a second command and one command per note, and helps less often than a line under every destructive permission dialog.
named the widget stakes-widget ("Stakes")

stamped pass: Stakes is the only idea that changes a decision the person makes alone: it measures what a yes would lose and writes it into the permission dialog, which no widget touches, with every call it needs present in the types file.
